News.title: How to manage debt when planning an earlier retirement
News.content:
Thinking about borrowing and repayments in retirement

As people approach or move through retirement, it can be helpful to take a step back and look at how any ongoing financial commitments fit into their wider plans. Different types of borrowing can work in different ways, and understanding the basics may help people feel more informed about their options.

Some financial commitments, such as mortgages or regular household bills, are typically linked to essential living costs, while others may be more flexible. Having an overview of regular outgoings and how long they are expected to run for may form part of broader financial planning considerations.

If someone has more than one borrowing arrangement for example, mortgages, credit cards or personal loans, they may find it helpful to consider how manageable these commitments are alongside their retirement income. In some cases, people review how their repayments are structured or how many separate commitments they have, although what is suitable will depend on individual circumstances and will not be right for everyone.

It's important to remember that different options can have different long term implications, including the total amount repaid over time or the impact on future financial flexibility. Information about borrowing and repayments is widely available, but individual circumstances vary, so people may wish to seek independent guidance before making changes. Free, independent debt advice is also available from organisations such as MoneyHelper or StepChange, which some may find useful when considering their wider financial position.

The options mentioned here are for general information only and are not financial advice. They form part of the wider considerations someone may take into account when reviewing their financial position and are not services provided or advised on by the Telegraph or Royal London Equity Release Advisers.

News.title: Hepatitis B
News.content:
Key facts

Hepatitis B is a viral infection that attacks the liver and can cause both acute and chronic disease

The virus is most commonly transmitted from mother to child during birth and delivery, in early childhood, as well as through contact with blood or other body fluids during sex with an infected partner, unsafe injections or exposures to sharp instruments.

Hepatitis B can be prevented by vaccines

It is estimated there are 1.2 million new infections each year and around 1.1 million deaths

Overview

Hepatitis B is a liver infection caused by a virus, which can be either short-term or long-term. Hepatitis B is a major global health concern and is most prevalent in the western Pacific, Africa and south east Asia. The infection can lead to chronic illness, significantly increasing the risk of death from cirrhosis and liver cancer.

Adults are more likely to develop the acute form of the disease, while children are more likely to have the chronic form.

Signs and symptoms

Most people do not experience any symptoms when newly infected. However, some people can have acute illness and symptoms can include:

a high temperature

tiredness

pain in the abdomen

nausea and vomiting

yellowing of the skin and whites of the eyes (jaundice)

dark urine

Dangers and complications

Most people do not have any lasting problems after having a hepatitis B infection. However, chronic hepatitis B can cause liver damage (cirrhosis) and increase the risk of getting liver cancer if left untreated. It is important to take any medicine prescribed and attend regular check-ups to ensure the liver is functioning properly.

Transmission

The virus is spread through contact with infected bodily fluids, such as blood, saliva, vaginal fluids, and semen. In areas where it is most prevalent, it is mainly spread from mother to child at birth or from an infected child to an uninfected child during the first five years of life.

Hepatitis B can also be spread through needlestick injuries, tattooing, piercing, and exposure to infected blood and body fluids. Transmission can occur through the reuse of contaminated needles and syringes.

Treatment

There is no specific treatment for acute hepatitis B. Care focuses on treating the symptom including administering fluids to prevent dehydration. Medicines, such as painkillers, can be offered to help with symptoms. Chronic hepatitis B can be treated with oral medicines, such as tenofovir or entecavir.

Treatment can slow the advance of cirrhosis, reduce cases of liver cancer, and improve long-term survival. Most people who start hepatitis B treatment must continue it for life. A liver specialist may be required to monitor the liver.

Prevention

Hepatitis B is preventable with a vaccine. In the UK babies receive three doses of the vaccine as part of the routine immunisation schedule. Babies born to mothers who have the infection receive six doses, with the first administered within 24 hours of birth. The vaccine will prevent the baby developing the disease.

Booster vaccines are not usually required for people who have completed the three-dose vaccination.

Other ways to reduce risk:

practice safe sex using condoms and reducing the number of sexual partners

avoid sharing needles or any equipment used for injecting drugs, piercing or tattooing

wash hands thoroughly with soap and water after coming into contact with blood, body fluids or contaminated surfaces

get a hepatitis B vaccine if working in a healthcare setting

use a condom

avoid sharing razors, toothbrushes and needles with others

History

While it had been recognised since the 1940s that there were two different types of hepatitis – A and B – it was the discovery of the “Australia” antigen in 1965 that kickstarted research into hepatitis. Today, it is recognised that there are five main types of the disease – A, B, C, D and E. They all cause liver disease but they differ in terms of transmission, disease severity and geographical spread, with types B and C causing the greatest disease burden.

A hepatitis B vaccine was first developed in the early 1970s and blood banks began screening donated blood for the disease at around the same time. Since 2017 all babies in the UK receive the hepatitis B vaccine as part of the routine immunisation schedule

Sports.title: ‘I forgot to remind you…’ – York City owner bizarrely takes break from promotion party to troll bottom-half strugglers
Sports.content:
THE OWNER of National League winners York City trolled a club he once wished “all the best” in a bizarre outburst following his team’s dramatic return to the EFL.

Matt Uggla used expletives in a post on X brutally criticising Yeovil Town, who he was associated with in 2023.





York faced Rochdale away in a title decider on Saturday – the hosts thought they’d won it in the 95th minute following Manu Dieseruvwe’s goal, but Josh Stones dramatically equalised for York eight minutes later to snatch the trophy back.

Wild celebrations followed, both online and on the pitch.

But York owner Uggla took to social media to troll Yeovil Town, who he used to have ties with.

He replied to Yeovil’s full-time post on X after the Glovers lost 4-1 to Solihull Moors on the final day.

Uggla wrote: “I’m so so sorry guys, in all the commotion I completely forgot to remind you…. YOU LOT ARE REALLY S***! Enjoy the abyss.”

The random swipe at Yeovil after York made a historic and unbelievable return to the Football League confused fans, with many reacting to the outburst.

One wrote: “Money can’t buy class.”



A second posted: “Cheers Matt good to see you are gracious in victory.”

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

While a third said: “Matt just shut up all that time partying and we’re still in your head.”

Uggla was part of a consortium linked to buying Yeovil in 2023 – he and former rugby union star Paul Sackey formed “SU Glovers” and took on stewardship of the Somerset club.

However the takeover appeared to collapse after Yeovil’s relegation to the National League South.

The owner is seemingly no longer a fan of the club despite a statement in 2023 saying: “We wish you guys all the best and we will definitely watch from afar and wish the club success. Glovers for life.”



His bizarre and hate-filled social media outburst begs to differ with his previous claim.

Matt Uggla is the son of Canadian finance entrepreneur Lance Uggla who has a reported net worth of over £100million.

Matt bought York City with his mum, Julie-Anne, in the summer of 2023.

After missing out via the National League play-offs last season despite achieving a staggering 96 points, the Yorkshire club went one better this year.

The title race with Rochdale went right down to the final day in one of the most dramatic football matches ever played.



York’s 103rd-minute equaliser took them to an incredible 108 points and sealed the title in Uggla’s third season backing the club.

The victory was followed by a crazy 24-hour celebration involving pubs, partying and lots of social media posts.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

One York player made headlines after landing a huge left hook on a Rochdale fan.

But there seems to be no love lost between Uggla and former Championship club Yeovil Town.

Sports.title: Why are Man Utd wearing a special kit with (RED) as their sponsor vs Brentford?
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED continue their hot pursuit of Champions League football for next season with a huge match against Brentford TONIGHT – and they’ll be doing it with a special kit.

Three points for United would see them go three clear of Liverpool and Aston Villa who are both on 58 points.



But more importantly, it would all but seal them a place in the Champions League next season as they’ll be 11 points ahead of sixth-place Brighton.



However, the Bees are chasing European football themselves so they will most certainly not roll over easily.

Plus, they’ll be determined to stop a run of five consecutive Premier League draws, with their last win coming at the back end of February.

But while most will be concentrating on the football, others will be wondering why United have a special kit with a different front-of-shirt sponsor, and SunSport can explain the reason behind it.

Why are Man Utd wearing a special kit with (RED) as their sponsor?

Manchester United and (RED) has partnered with MatchWorn Shirt (MWS) to launch a unique fundraising initiative which gives fans the chance to own exclusive Manchester United match-worn shirts from their favourite stars.



Following the match, a full set of match-worn, issued and signed shirts, including those from the starting eleven and the substitutes will be made available to fans and collectors.

Founded by Bono & Bobby Shriver in 2006, (RED) partners with the world’s most iconic brands such as Manchester United to raise money, heat and urgency for global health crises.

To date, (RED) has generated over $800million (approx £590m) for Global Fund, helping more than 350m people worldwide.

Tijmen Zonderwijk, co-founder at MatchWornShirt, said: “These shirts represent the very best of football – moments on the pitch transformed into meaningful impact off it. By bringing fans closer to the game they love, we’re turning that passion into something bigger, helping to raise critical funds and awareness for life-saving global health programmes around the world.”



Kate Charles, Managing Director of (RED), said: “This collection shows how purpose-driven partnerships can turn the power of sport into real-world impact. Each shirt tells a story from the pitch, while also helping to fund life-saving global health programs in communities where they are needed most.”

Where can you buy Man Utd’s special edition shirt?

The special kit will be made available to fans and collectors via the MWS website and app.

Fans have the opportunity to get their hands on these special shirts from Monday, April 27 until Saturday, May 2.

Fans can learn more about the auction and participate via www.mws.com

Net proceeds from the auction will go in part to support (RED)’s mission to combat global health crises.



When else did Man Utd partner up with (RED)?

Manchester United partnered up with (Red) for their home clash against West Ham last May.

The special edition changed top was also used for United’s Women’s WSL clash with Arsenal.

Sports.title: What do Man Utd need to qualify for Champions League?
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED are closing in on Champions League qualification.

The Red Devils have not been in Europe’s elite competition since the 2023/24 season, when they crashed out in the group stage.



Man Utd legend Michael Carrick took interim charge at Old Trafford when Ruben Amorim was sacked in early January.



The legendary midfielder has taken the club from 7th to third in the Premier League table and is well in the frame for the job on a permanent basis.

Carrick looks set to lead United to a Champions League return, but when can they officially seal their entry to the competition?

What do Man Utd need to qualify for Champions League?

Like last season, the top five in the Premier League table will secure Champions League football.

Man Utd are currently on 58 points with 15 points left to play for this season.

The Red Devils next play Brentford and a victory over the Bees would put them on the cusp of qualification.

Should United win on Monday night, they will move to 61 points and their status in Europe’s elite competition could be confirmed before they host Liverpool on Sunday, if Brighton and Bournemouth fail to win this weekend.

With plenty of permutations to play out, the long and short of it is that United need six more points from their remaining five games to guarantee Champions League football, whatever happens.

27: Brentford (h) – 8pm

Sports.title: Kai Havertz injury update with Arsenal star set to miss crunch Champions League clash after KO against Newcastle
Sports.content:
ARSENAL remain optimistic that Kai Havertz will return from injury before the end of the Premier League season.

The 26-year-old was forced off after just 33 minutes against Newcastle on Saturday.





He appeared to suffer a muscular injury, putting the remainder of his campaign in doubt.

Arsenal are understood to be hopeful that he will recover in time for the last part of the Premier League title run-in.

The Athletic reports that early assessments have been more positive than initial fears.

And while he is expected to be ruled out for the Champions League semi-final first leg against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and the upcoming Prem clash with Fulham at the weekend, the Gunners hope that he will return within weeks.

Havertz has been limited to just 20 appearances for Arsenal this season due to injuries.

He appeared to suffer a groin issue on Saturday after starting in attack against Newcastle.

Eberechi Eze was also forced off during the match, but later insisted that it was just a precaution.

At full-time, Mikel Arteta said: “We don’t think it’s too much.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“We have to wait and see if they’re going to be available for Wednesday.”

Eze scored the decisive goal as Arsenal clinched a 1-0 win over Newcastle.

They returned to the top of the Premier League table as a result, moving three points above Manchester City with four games to play.

Speaking after the match, Arteta admitted: “I’m really happy with the win.

“We talked about game one and how important that was. We probably should have finished it with a bigger margin in certain moments of the game.



“But when it’s 1-0 it’s always tough because they have quality, because they brought so many good players from the bench as well.

“When we don’t finish the action, especially the open ones that we had, the margin is going to be smaller.”

Sports.title: Man Utd set for major injury boost as star hints he is in squad for Brentford after three months out
Sports.content:
PATRICK DORGU is in line for a return to the Manchester United squad for the first time since the end of January.

The left-sided star has been out with injury since the dramatic 3-2 win over Arsenal in Michael Carrick‘s second match in charge as interim (this season).





He had scored to put United ahead in that game but was forced off with 10 minutes still to play.

Now, just hours before Brentford are welcomed to Old Trafford, Dorgu has posted a hint at being involved again.

He put up a pre-game graphic on Instagram with the words “Patience, work, faith. God answers prayer” written on it.

Dorgu’s pic includes all the matchday details that players often upload when they’re going to be involved.

Speaking last week, Carrick himself said Dorgu was on the mend and closing in on a return.

He said: “Patrick’s looking to get back closer to the group in a very small part, which is fantastic, because he’s worked so hard over a period of time now.

“So it’ll be good to have him back in and around the group within the next week or so.”

If he is picked in anyway to face Brentford it would be an even quicker recovery than the boss had been hoping for.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

United‘s last Premier League game – the 1-0 win over Chelsea – saw a patchwork backline keep a clean sheet.

That included Ayden Heaven and full-back Noussair Mazraoui in the middle of defence.

Luke Shaw has had to play without rest on the left with Tyrell Malacia fit to be a sub again but hardly featuring.

Dorgu had hit a fine patch of form before his injury, scoring three and assisting twice in seven Prem games.

That covered the end of Ruben Amorim‘s tenure, Darren Fletcher‘s brief caretaker spell, and the start of Carrick’s second stint in charge.

Sports.title: Chelsea will make contact with Alonso with ex-Real Madrid boss on three-man manager shortlist after Rosenior sacking
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are planning talks with a trio of managers after sacking Liam Rosenior.

Xabi Alonso and Marco Silva, the Fulham manager, have been added to their shortlist after SunSport revealed their interest in departing Bournemouth manager Andoni Iraola last week.





Iraola, 43, has confirmed he will leave The Cherries at the end of the season, while Silva – who has been with rivals Fulham since 2021 – is out of contract in the summer.

The Portuguese, 48, was offered a new deal at the back end of last year but is yet to commit to an extension and talks are continuing.

Alonso, 44, is out of work having left Real Madrid in January, just seven months after his appointment.

The former Liverpool midfielder, who has been linked with replacing Arne Slot at Anfield, previously masterminded an invincible Bundesliga title win with Bayer Leverkusen, where he also won the German Cup.

READ MORE ON CHELSEA FRANK ME LATER Lampard warned not to take 'insane' Chelsea job by former team-mate

Chelsea, who reached the FA Cup final with a win over Leeds on Sunday in their first game since sacking Rosenior, will not put a timeline on a new appointment.

However, the club conceded that a period of “self-reflection” was needed following the latest change in the dugout, which has left their American owners searching for a fifth permanent manager since their takeover 2022.

The two previous appointments, Rosenior and Enzo Maresca, arrived without any high-level managerial experience.

Maresca had only managed in the Championship, winning the league with Leicester, while Rosenior had worked in the Championship and enjoyed a successful spell with sister club Strasbourg in Ligue 1.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Given the significance of the next appointment after two sackings this season, Chelsea are in no rush to make a snap decision.

A host of other names, including Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann, have been linked with the post though his appointment would require Chelsea to wait until after this summer’s World Cup – a risk they may want to avoid.

Calum McFarlane, the club’s former Under-21s manager who was promoted to the first team staff after taking interim charge before Rosenior arrived, will be in the dugout for the remainder of the season.

Silva and Iraola have both impressed at mid-table Prem sides, taking Bournemouth and Fulham from risking relegation to stable and competitive with the European place-chasing pack.



It all comes in a stacked but moveable managerial market.

Manchester United, should they choose not to give Michael Carrick the permanent gig at Old Trafford, will also be searching for a new boss.

Eddie Howe’s tenure at Newcastle could yet be coming to an end as well as he faces increasing scrutiny.

Real themselves might need to replace Alvaro Arbeloa, and there is a host of international managers who could fancy their chances back in the domestic game after the World Cup.

Thomas Tuchel – despite signing a new contract with England – and Mauricio Pochettino have all been linked with club jobs this year.

Sports.title: How Man Utd ace George Best’s secret ‘red splodge’ artwork is set to make barmaid £35k after bizarre tale of friendship
Sports.content:
GEORGE Best was famous for his gifts on the pitch as a Manchester United legend, but less is known about his hidden talent for painting.

There is only one example of his artwork that has ever been uncovered, and in a bizarre tale, the “red splodge” piece is now set to make a mystery barmaid named Hayley £35k when it heads to auction.



George befriended Hayley when he lived at Champneys Forest Mere Spa during his divorce from wife Alex in 2003.

She told how he would sit in the bar drinking coffee with her before she booked him a taxi to take him to a local favourite pub, The Half Moon.



And she revealed the Northern Irish charmer painted a picture in red to match a feature wall in her bedroom, “which he knew all about”.

Best was rumoured to have painted several pieces while in rehabilitation, but none of his amateur art has been discovered until now.

Bartender Hayley said: “I was renovating my first flat at the time and I had just painted a red feature wall in my bedroom, which he knew all about.

“He came down one morning with a picture he had painted for my bedroom wall as a gift. He specifically had done it in reds to match my new bedroom.

“He said it was abstract, and it was three faces.



“He had already signed the front in paint, but I asked him to sign the back, which is when he wrote ‘Lots of love, to my favourite Hayley, George Best.

“I hugged and thanked him as I found it very moving at the time, and it’s been kept safe in my ownership ever since.”

Best, who died in 2005 aged just 59 after battling booze, lived at the spa resort in Liphook, Hampshire, for two years after his marriage with wife Alex broke down in 2003.

The troubled former footballer arrived at Forest Mere, accompanied by his agent Philip Hughes, and checked into the £200-a-night retreat after returning from a holiday to Malta with Alex.

His 31-year-old wife abandoned the couple’s holiday following newspaper reports published over the weekend that claimed Best was having an affair.



He was pictured drinking wine alone at the couple’s hotel, sparking fears that he may have damaged his new liver, less than a year after a life-saving transplant.

Earlier that year, the footballer was arrested on suspicion of assault at a pub in Walton-on-the-Hill, Surrey, but was later released without charge.

He was ‘lonely and isolated’

Now, 23 years later, the painting he created in the wake of his marriage breaking down is set to go under the hammer at Sportingold Auctions in Barnsley, South Yorkshire, on April 30.

The lucky buyer will get the one-of-a-kind art piece, which was done on an artist card, as well as various certificates of authenticity.

The original Best artwork has been authenticated by the football legend’s long-term friend and agent, Phil Hughes.



It includes provenance letters from the original owner to whom George gifted the piece, as well as from another member of staff who worked with Hayley.

In her letter, Hayley said: “I began my employment at Champneys Forest Mere health farm in January 2002, and my employment ended in October 2004.

“The current owner at the time was close friends with the late George Best and invited him to reside there and use it as his full-time residence during his divorce from Alex Best.



“I worked on the bar there during my time of employment. George would come and sit at the bar every morning with his Daily Mail, order a coffee and sit and do his crossword.

“We had very similar senses of humour, so we got on really well and built a friendship very quickly. He’d spend a couple of hours at the bar every morning, and we’d do the crossword together and chat a lot.

“George came across as lonely and isolated at the time, so I think our friendship gave him companionship that was needed at that point in his life.

“I’d normally then book him a taxi, and he’d go to a local pub – The Half Moon was his favourite.

“He used to like to leave before the bar and restaurant got busy for the lunch sitting, as the spa day guests would arrive.



“He’d then return around 3pm and sit and chat to me until I finished.

“We spent a lot of time together and knew all about what was going on in each other’s lives at the time.”

A Sportingold spokesman said: “Quite simply, the Manchester United and sporting superstar had unknown depths — a truly stunning piece of work.”

Sports.title: Europa League specialist Igor Jesus a potential needle mover as season nears dramatic climax
Sports.content:
NOTTINGHAM FOREST took another huge stride towards safety last Friday.

Vitor Pereira’s side swaggered to a 5-0 win over Sunderland at the Stadium of Light to take their total to 39 points and maintain an advantage over West Ham and Tottenham, even after both relegation rivals celebrated victories of their own on Saturday.



Morgan Gibbs-White (£4.6m) continued his fine form with another goal but it was Igor Jesus (£3.3m) who earned the most Dream Team points on Tyneside.



The Brazilian striker opened the floodgates in the 17th minute when he forced Trai Hume (£2.6m) to score an own goal with a back-post header, registering a fantasy assist in the process.

In the 34th minute, Jesus picked out Gibbs-White with a smart knock-down to make it two assists on the night.

And just three minutes later he scored a goal of his own, a composed volley, as the visitors ran riot.

With the result effectively settled, Jesus was replaced midway through the second half, by which time he had collected 14 points (despite a yellow card).

The 25-year-old now ranks eighth among Dream Team forwards with 229 points to his name, one more than Viktor Gyokeres (£4.5m).

He has scored 15 goals and provided seven assists in 2025/26 so far.

Granted, just five of his goals have come in the Premier League but he’s been prolific in the other competitions with ten goals in 12 games.



Jesus is the top scorer in the Europa League this campaign with seven goals at a strike rate of one every 88 minutes.

This Thursday, he will have the chance to add to his impressive European tally when Forest take on Aston Villa in the first leg of their semi-final at the City Ground.

Jesus is already the best-performing striker of Gameweek 33 and he has every chance of maintaining his status given Forest are one of just four teams with a second fixture to fulfil before the next deadline.

The East Midlanders will also double up in Gameweek 34.



Pereira’s side are scheduled to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge this coming weekend before making the short trip to Villa Park for the second leg of their Europa League semi.

Dream Team bosses who took a punt on Jesus in Gameweek 33 have been handsomely rewarded and it’s not unreasonable to expect further returns in Gameweek 34.

He is currently the fifth-most popular recruit ahead of Friday’s deadline — his ownership has risen to 7.2%.

Sports.title: Christian Eriksen told Ruben Amorim exactly how he felt just before Man Utd sack
Sports.content:
Christian Eriksen told Ruben Amorim exactly how he felt just before Man Utd sack

Christian Eriksen will see two of his former sides come up against each other in the Premier League on Monday night.

View 2 Images Christian Eriksen left United in the summer transfer window, and has since spoken about Ruben Amorim. (Image: Alex Livesey, Getty Images)

Christian Eriksen will have particular reason to tune in when two of his former employers go head-to-head in the Premier League on Monday evening. Manchester United welcome Brentford to Old Trafford, with the midfielder having turned out for both clubs.

‌



Eriksen departed United last summer and has since issued a scathing verdict on former boss Ruben Amorim. The Portuguese manager failed to make his mark at United and departed in early January.

‌



Just days prior to Amorim's departure, Eriksen hit out at certain remarks made by the manager. The boss was publicly critical of his squad, branding them the 'worst team' in the club's history.

‌



Michael Carrick reveals Sir Jim Ratcliffe meeting as his Man Utd future hangs in the balance READ MORE :

11 players could be forced to sit out Man Utd vs Brentford as Michael Carrick gets timely boost READ MORE :

"That didn't help. Yeah, that didn't help at all. I mean, that was not ... I don't think that helped the players at all," Eriksen told the Sunday Times back in December.

"Some stuff you can say inside and it's not too clever to say outside, to put extra pressure and put an extra label on the players who were already trying to do their best.

"I don't think that helped at all, no. Then if he's right or wrong, whatever, but I think for us it was a bit of like, 'Oh, here we go again. Another headline.'"

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

When asked what he made of Amorim as a coach, the midfielder added: "He came in with his ideas. He tried to change things as you still see, tried to get it his way.

"Certain players for certain positions, for a certain style of play, that's how he sees success. He has to change a lot because the players were not used to that system.

‌



"Also, historically, United always liked a different system. And yeah, he's been very honest and also, yeah, honest with me from the beginning. Very, very, very honest, I would say."

View 2 Images Ruben Amorim left Manchester United back in January. (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Following Amorim's departure, United appointed Michael Carrick on a temporary basis. They have won eight of his 12 matches in charge, rising to third in the Premier League and practically securing Champions League qualification for next season.

Article continues below

Eriksen, meanwhile, signed for German outfit Wolfsburg in the summer and is a regular starter in their line-up this campaign, recently wearing the captain's armband. The midfielder spent six months at Brentford between January and July 2022, as he returned to action following a cardiac arrest 18 months prior.

He subsequently joined United, racking up a total of 107 appearances across three years with the club before departing on a free transfer in the summer.

Sports.title: Arsenal braced for Atletico Madrid pitch issues after Tottenham and Barcelona complaints
Sports.content:
Arsenal braced for Atletico Madrid pitch issues after Tottenham and Barcelona complaints

Arsenal face Atletico Madrid in the first leg of their Champions League semi-final on Wednesday, with the La Liga side hoping to continue their impressive home record

View 2 Images Arsenal are expecting issues with the pitch at the Metropolitano Stadium

Arsenal will be braced for another pitch battle at Atletico Madrid.

‌



Gunners boss Mikel Arteta faces a tough semi final against Atletico on Wednesday night as the Spanish giants have turned their home into a fortress this season.

‌



Tottenham complained the pitch was watered too heavily before their last 16 tie in March and that led to players slipping on the wet surface. Barcelona boss Hansi Flick said the grass was too long before their quarter final to try and slow the game down.

‌



It will be a genuine concern for Arsenal ahead of their semi-final tie as Atletico are underdogs but their 70,000 capacity Metropolitano Stadium could be a huge weapon. The crowd will be passionate and lively while manager Diego Simeone has vast experience of making life difficult for opponents.

Arsenal target Julian Alvarez wanted by rival club as transfer approach emerges READ MORE :

Gary Lineker names 'tricky' fixture that could cost Arsenal the Premier League title READ MORE :

There are strict UEFA rules on the state of the pitch which say “the home club must make every reasonable effort to ensure that the pitch is in the best possible condition” and they will undergo strict pre-match checks.

UEFA’s Article 34 also states: “The home club must respect the pitch-cutting guidelines for natural grass pitches. The height of the grass must not exceed 30mm and the entire playing surface must be cut to the same height.

‌



“The height of the grass should be the same for both the training sessions and the match. If deemed necessary by the referee or the UEFA match delegate, the home club may be required to reduce the height of the grass for the match and training sessions.

“The pitch-watering schedule must be communicated by the home club at the organisational meeting. The pitch must be watered evenly and not only in certain areas.

View 2 Images Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky had a nightmare on the pitch which Spurs claimed was watered too heavily (Image: Alberto Gardin/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

‌



“As a general rule, pitch watering must finish 60 minutes before kick-off. However, upon the decision of the home club, pitch watering may also take place after that time: between 10 and 5 minutes before kick-off; and/or during half-time, for a maximum of 5 minutes.”

That states that Atletico can water the pitch just before kick-off and therefore Arsenal are certain to keep an eye on what happens.

Meanwhile, Arsenal are still waiting on defender Jurrien Timber to return to fitness. The Dutch defender has been a big miss for the Gunners because of a groin injury and he has yet to step up his training levels.

‌



But Timber has done some work and the hope is that he will be able to kick on and be available for the run-in even though his continued absence is a worry for Arsenal and also Holland ahead of the World Cup.

Eberechi Eze has insisted that he expects to be fit after a scare against Newcastle but Kai Havertz is likely to be out for longer but it is not expected to be a serious lay-off.

Sports.title: Chelsea next manager: Xabi Alonso added to shortlist as opening contact made
Sports.content:
Chelsea next manager: Xabi Alonso added to shortlist as opening contact made

After sacking Liam Rosenior and appointing Calum McFarlane on an interim basis, Chelsea are searching for their next permanent manager, and three names on their shortlist have emerged

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso is on Chelsea's shortlist (Image: Ricardo Larreina/Europa Press via Getty Images)

Chelsea will make checks on both Xabi Alonso and Marco Silva after contacting Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola in their search for a new manager. The Blues sacked Liam Rosenior last week on the back of suffering five consecutive Premier League defeats, leaving their Champions League hopes in tatters.

‌



Calum McFarlane will take charge of first-team duties until the end of this season after guiding Chelsea to the FA Cup final with Sunday's 1-0 victory over Leeds. McFarlane will then be a replaced by a permanent successor to Rosenior, who lasted just three months in the Stamford Bridge hot seat.

‌



It emerged on Monday that Chelsea have made contact with Iraola, 43, who's already confirmed to be leaving Bournemouth upon the expiry of his contract in June. But the Spaniard isn't the only manager under consideration, the Telegraph report.

‌



Fulham boss Silva, who like Iraola is out of contract this summer, is also set to be contacted. As is Alonso, who was sacked by Real Madrid in January after just seven months in charge, and the former Liverpool midfielder is under the same representation as compatriot Iraola.

Trevoh Chalobah hits back at Chelsea critics after response to Liam Rosenior accusations READ MORE :

Those three aren't the only coaches on Chelsea's shortlist, though, with other unnamed candidates also being discussed. Their group of five sporting directors will spearhead the process of appointing the club's sixth permanent manager since Chelsea were purchased by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital's consortium in 2022.

‌



The Blues have a week until they play again, hosting relegation-threatened Nottingham Forest next Monday afternoon. While Alonso and Iraola are both available for hire in the summer as things stand, Silva's future at Fulham remains undecided.

Who should Chelsea appoint as their next manager? Let us know your pick in the comments section.

View 2 Images Chelsea plan to speak to Marco Silva's camp, having already contacted that of Andoni Iraola (Image: GLYN KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



When asked last week if there'd been any progress regarding his future, the Portuguese snapped: "No. Why is it different this week? It is not at all.

"It is the same and the same answer that I said to you already last week, it is the same. I will not make, every single week, comments about [my future].

"When something comes new, we are going to tell from ourselves, myself and the club. Everything what I need, or the club needs to do with me is going to be between me and the club."

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham's reason for snubbing Man Utd transfer despite private tour of Old Trafford
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham's reason for snubbing Man Utd transfer despite private tour of Old Trafford

Manchester United fell short in their efforts to tempt Jude Bellingham to Old Trafford despite a private tour of the club and the promise of early riches

View 2 Images Jude Bellingham rejected the chance to join Manchester United six years ago despite the club's committed attempts (Image: CRISTINA QUICLER, AFP via Getty Images)

Virtually every major European giant was vying for the signature of Jude Bellingham in the summer of 2020. Manchester United were no exception and extended an invitation to the Birmingham City wonderkid to visit their Carrington training ground in a bid to win him over.

‌



Bellingham was still only 16 when he was shown around what could have become his new home alongside his parents in March 2020. The trip included a meeting with Old Trafford legend Sir Alex Ferguson, while former chief executive Ed Woodward was understood to have played a significant role in orchestrating the visit.

‌



As it transpired, the now-22-year-old snubbed the advances of several heavyweights, including United and Chelsea, opting instead to join Borussia Dortmund. It's fair to say the decision has paid dividends for the England star, who spent three years in Germany before completing a move to Real Madrid in a deal potentially rising to £113million.

‌



Sky Sports reported at the time that Bellingham had been impressed by what he witnessed at Carrington. This is despite the training facilities having undergone a significant overhaul since Sir Jim Ratcliffe assumed control of the club's day-to-day operations.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

As for why he rejected United, it was reported Bellingham's parents, Denise and Mark, believed his development would be better served in the Bundesliga. Dortmund highlighted Jadon Sancho as proof of how rapidly young players can flourish in Germany following his rapid rise after departing Manchester City.

‌



Jude Bellingham buys stake in cricket team as Real Madrid star joins The Hundred READ MORE :

Top five salaries in Premier League and La Liga compared with Erling Haaland only third READ MORE :

It seems the Bellingham family concurred, demonstrated by the fact Jude's younger brother, Jobe, also now represents the Black and Yellows. The elder sibling was indeed handed immediate opportunities to shine in front of the Yellow Wall, chances he may not have been afforded had he moved to Old Trafford.

Former Birmingham City CEO Xuandong Ren told Mundo Deportivo Bellingham declined a substantially higher wage when he rejected United and others. That was one of the earliest indicators regarding Bellingham's determination to chart the course he imagined.

"Jude did not make any decision based on money," said Ren in 2022. "They were offering much more salary compared to the rest. Maybe double. He was going to be guaranteed millions in the bank and he didn't take it. That's not normal for a player at all."

‌



View 2 Images Bellingham was arguably the most in-demand prospect on the planet when he left Birmingham in 2020 (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

That story once more illustrates the player's dedication to being the architect of his own future. And it suggests United were perhaps waging a losing battle to attract the midfielder at that point in his career.

Bellingham and Sancho were team-mates at Dortmund for one season before the latter made the switch to Old Trafford. However, by the time Bellingham's signature came back on the market in 2023, Sancho found himself firmly out in the cold at United.

‌

That decline in fortunes may have influenced Bellingham's decision not to follow his friend's path. Then again, it's equally possible the allure of the Bernabeu just proved too strong to resist and United were once more left trailing in the pecking order.

Bellingham, whose Real contract runs until 2029, hasn't sparkled this season quite like he did during his opening two Spanish campaigns. However, having battled through several injury problems this term, Birmingham's former prodigy will get his opportunity for redemption when England head to World Cup 2026 this summer.

Sports.title: Four men charged after incident at Rochdale vs York City title decider
Sports.content:
Four men charged after incident at Rochdale vs York City title decider

Four men have been charged over a reported incident after York City scored a dramatic equaliser to win the National League title

View 2 Images York City celebrate the team's promotion and title victory with the trophy following their draw against Rochdale (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Four men have been charged in connection with an incident which was reported at the end of the Rochdale AFC v York City match on Saturday, April 25. Police were called following the game between both sides at the weekend.

‌



Greater Manchester Police have confirmed on Monday that four men will appear before magistrates later this year following the alleged incident. Kiean Sultan, 18, of Thirlmere Drive, Middleton, has been charged with pitch encroachment and Section 4 of the Public Order Act.

‌



Aaron Dawson, 31, of Smithies Street, Heywood, has been charged with two counts of Section 4B of the Public Order Act. Sam Manicolo, 18, of Hollins Drive, Middleton, has been charged with pitch encroachment. Thomas Coleman, 23, of Blenheim Street, Rochdale, has been charged with pitch encroachment.

‌



Rochdale vs York ends in dramatic scenes after pitch invasions and controversial goal READ MORE :

One man was initially arrested at the scene but later de-arrested. All four men have been bailed and are due to appear at Manchester and Salford Magistrates on August 18.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Saturday's match saw York score an incredible 103rd-minute equaliser to win the National League title. The Minstermen had one hand on the trophy heading into stoppage time at the Crown Oil Arena with a draw enough to seal promotion.

‌



Yet with time running out, the match descended into pandemonium. Mani Dieseruvwe netted a superb header in the 96th minute for Rochdale, triggering jubilant scenes and a pitch invasion. A victory for Dale would see them promoted as champions, and they believed they'd found a crucial goal.

View 2 Images York City sealed promotiom with their dramatic draw against Rochdale (Image: Getty Images)

Veteran forward Ian Henderson came off the bench to deliver a moment of brilliance. The 40-year-old curled the ball into the far post with the outside of his foot, and Dieseruvwe rose highest to power a header past York City shot stopper Harrison Male.

‌



Rochdale fans flooded onto the pitch to celebrate what they assumed would be the title. Following a five-minute delay, supporters were cleared from the pitch and play continued.

York then pushed players forward and scored an astonishing equaliser in the 103rd minute through Josh Stones, to clinch the title in sensational fashion.

Callum Howe's header was cleared off the line before the ball fell to Stones at the far post. He forced the ball towards the goal, though there were doubts over whether it had actually crossed the line, with York players insistent they'd secured the winner.

Article continues below

The officials awarded the goal, and the travelling away fans surged onto the pitch. It lead to absolute bedlam as York players, staff and supporters celebrated frantically on the sidelines.

Sports.title: Arsenal target Julian Alvarez wanted by rival club as transfer approach emerges
Sports.content:
Arsenal target Julian Alvarez wanted by rival club as transfer approach emerges

Julian Alvarez has been regularly linked with a return to the Premier League since leaving Manchester City and the Atletico Madrid star is once again attracting transfer interest

View 2 Images Barcelona are set to try and sign Julian Alvarez (Image: Europa Press via Getty Images)

Barcelona are said to have made contact with their domestic rivals Atletico Madrid over an ambitious deal for Julian Alvarez with the club set to prioritise signing a new No 9 this summer.

‌



Arsenal are known to be among Alvarez's many suitors, although Atletico are in a strong bargaining position given the 26-year-old is under contract until 2030. The striker's teams include a release clause set at a staggering €500m (£432.9m) - but that hasn't deterred interest from the reigning Spanish champions.

‌



Barcelona head coach, Hansi Flick, is understood to have asked the club hierarchy for a new striker this summer and Alvarez is the man the La Liga giants want to team up alongside Raphinha and Lamine Yamal next season.

‌



ESPN claim Barcelona have already made contact with Atletico in order to discover the club's stance on selling the player they signed from Manchester City back in 2024.

Arsenal set for financial boost as Ethan Nwaneri's Marseille nightmare worsens READ MORE :

Is Pep Guardiola about to quit Man City? The hints which suggest he might say goodbye READ MORE :

Though any prospective deal would fall some way short of the extraordinary figures in Alvarez's release clause, Barcelona would be willing to close a deal worth €95m (£82.2m) inclusive of add-ons. Atletico, on the other hand, are willing to counteract any proposals by offering Alvarez a lucrative new contract until 2032 to keep him at the club.

Barcelona have been plagued by financial difficulties in recent years and are currently operating just outside of La Liga's financial fair play rules, meaning there are limits on what they can spend.

‌



However, the club 'hope to move within the league's regulations' this summer, which would potentially help facilitate larger spends, while Alvarez's willingness to transfer could also aid any potential deal.

View 2 Images Alvarez is a wanted man with Arsenal among his many admirers (Image: Getty)

Barca are long-term admirers of Alvarez, who they scouted back in his River Plate days. The attacker is even viewed as the perfect long-term successor to Robert Lewandowski, who turns 38 later this year.

‌



Arsenal's interest in Alvarez emerged back in January and they too could court the Argentine in the summer in a bid to boost their firepower.

The Gunners signed Viktor Gyokeres for a significant fee from Sporting Lisbon back in the summer but Kai Havertz was selected ahead of him in the pivotal meeting with title rivals Manchester City earlier this month, while there has been plenty of scrutiny over the Swede's tally of 12 goals in 32 Premier League games as well as his all-round performances.

Sports.title: ‘Hamilton can still take wins’ – Brundle anticipates ‘big step' from Ferrari
Sports.content:
Ferrari will be among the teams likely to make a "big step" in performance at the Miami Grand Prix as they target closing the gap to Mercedes in what will still prove a “wide open” 2026 season at the front, says Sky Sports F1’s Martin Brundle.

Brundle believes that F1's return to action in the USA will be "like a relaunch of the season" after the sport's enforced April break with teams having had extended time to work on "dramatically changed and, hopefully, improved cars" with potential to shuffle the pecking order.

Mercedes will resume the campaign as clearly the team to beat after winning all three races so far with Drivers' Championship leader Kimi Antonelli and team-mate George Russell.

Ferrari and their drivers are closest to Mercedes in the standings with team-mates Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton separated by eight points in third and fourth place in the Drivers' Championship having engaged in entertaining wheel-to-wheel battles in both China and Japan.

On Hamilton, who broke his Grand Prix podium duck for Ferrari at the season's second round in Shanghai before a more difficult weekend at Suzuka when he finished sixth with Leclerc third, Brundle told Sky Sports News: "Lewis clearly enjoys these cars much more.

"Ferrari is more competitive and I think again will make a big step for Miami.

"Lewis obviously prefers this type of car to the seasons we had with the ground-effect cars that were smashing against the ground and were quite brutal things, it didn't seem to suit his style.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Formula 1 returning this weekend in Miami after an extended break, we look back at what happened during the first three races of the season

"But just his mood and just the way he's going about it, he just seems a lot happier because Ferrari is more competitive.

"He's got to beat Charles Leclerc if he's going to win the world championship in the other Ferrari, and others.

"Let's see if he can sustain that. If there's a sniff of a victory, I think Lewis is still very much capable of taking that."

Hamilton, when still at Mercedes, and Leclerc last won races in 2024 with Ferrari's own victory drought stretching back to October of that year, when Carlos Sainz won in Mexico City.

The season resumes with the year's second Sprint weekend in Miami, a race which McLaren have won in each of the past two seasons, although Mercedes remain favourites owing to their 100 per cent winning start to F1's new era of regulations in 2026.

But Brundle believes it is still too early in the new ruleset and car development for a definitive order to have emerged with 19 races left this season.

"I think it's totally wide open," said Brundle.

"We have got a Sprint weekend in Miami, so there are Sprint points to be won, Grand Prix points to be won.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle thinks Miami will feel like a relaunch to the season after rules updates and enforced break from F1

"This is going to ebb and flow. I see teams leapfrogging others with some upgrades because there is so much upside potential with these cars.

"Anybody I would say in the top four teams, any of those eight drivers, could win this year's world championship."

Sports.title: It's on! Contracts signed for Joshua vs Fury
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are set to meet in their long-awaited heavyweight mega-fight later this year.

Joshua will come back on July 25 in a tune-up bout against Kristian Prenga and then meet his great rival Fury.

Eddie Hearn, Joshua's promoter, posted on social media: "Signed, sealed and delivered! AJ vs Fury is on!"

He described it as "the biggest piece of business we've ever done but more importantly the one we've always wanted.

"Biggest year of AJ's career coming up, the comeback is on."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury grabbed the mic and bellowed a challenge for Anthony Joshua to fight him next!

Fury called out Joshua after his points victory over Arslanbek Makhmudov at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium earlier this month and revealed that he had signed for the all-British mega-fight.

Ring Magazine announced the fight was a "done deal" and would take place in "Q4, 2026" in a social media post on Monday.

Hearn previously told Sky Sports that November was the date they were targeting for Joshua's fight with Fury after his July comeback bout.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eddie Hearn revealed his plans for Anthony Joshua to fight Tyson Fury.

A decade of missed chances - How Joshua and Fury never happened

Joshua and Fury, two of the biggest names in British boxing, have circled one another for the best part of a decade. Fury first became a heavyweight world champion when he upset Wladimir Klitschko a decade ago. Joshua turned professional after winning Olympic gold at London 2012 and rocketed through the pro ranks.

But by the time Joshua picked up his first world title belt in 2016, Fury had stepped away from the sport.

Fury would eventually return and beat Deontay Wilder to become the WBC world champion. Joshua held the unified IBF, WBO and WBA championships and the two were close to fighting in an undisputed heavyweight championship fight.

It was not to be, Fury boxed a third fight with Wilder instead and Joshua lost to Oleksandr Usyk. The Ukrainian also defeated Fury, who retired again at the start of last year.

When Fury returned to beat Makhmudov in London earlier this month, Joshua was waiting for the all-clear to resume full training after sustaining injuries in a terrible accident in which two of his close friends and members of his team lost their lives. Joshua is now in camp working with his former rival Usyk, who has backed AJ to beat Fury.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 'AJ will beat Fury!' | Usyk on 'helping' Joshua in camp

With one more hurdle to clear for Joshua, Kristian Prenga on July 25, the two rivals will finally box in the most richly anticipated heavyweight bout the UK will have ever seen.

The exact date and location of the contest is yet to be confirmed but hopes will be high for another British stadium fight.

Fury vs AJ... and a Dua Lipa concert?

Sky Sports Boxing expert Andy Scott says:

"If you go to each part of this deal, everyone is saying the same thing: that Anthony Joshua will fight Tyson Fury this year.

"I've spoken to Spencer Brown from Gold Star promotions - who represents Tyson Fury - and he says 'go ahead and confirm it'.

"Tyson Fury came back successfully from his own retirement - he confirmed after the Arslanbek Makhmudov fight that he had signed his part of the deal.

"There was a little bit of disappointment that Joshua didn't join him in the ring and confirm that fight on the night.

"According to Turki, Spencer Brown, and Eddie Hearn that fight is done.

"There are lots of things still to go through. There isn't a confirmed venue, and AJ still needs to go through his own comeback fight. Brown has confirmed that it's a two-fight deal.

"I don't know if they're pulling my leg here, but I'm hearing that Turki has stipulated that Dua Lipa needs to perform at the fight! If you're listening, Dua, clear your diary!

"We aren't there yet - but we are very close now. AJ needs to come through his next fight, and then all roads lead to Joshua vs Fury next year."

Sports.title: Joshua sets comeback fight for July 25
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua will return to boxing in a comeback bout on July 25 in Saudi Arabia.

The former unified world champion will fight Kristian Prenga in Riyadh this summer.

It will be Joshua's first contest since returning to training after a car accident in Nigeria in December saw two of his close friends die.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eddie Hearn reveals the latest on Anthony Joshua’s fight plans as negotiations with Tyson Fury advance.

The official announcement of AJ's comeback fight has been accompanied by confirmation from promoters Turki Alashikh and Eddie Hearn that Joshua will finally fight his great rival Tyson Fury later this year.

Joshua said: "It's no secret I've taken some time to consolidate and rebuild to be ready for stepping back into the ring and today is the next step on that journey. I'm delighted to have agreed a multi-fight deal starting with July 25 in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

"I'm looking forward to competing and picking up where I left oﬀ. As I said: The landlord will collect his rent. That is certain."

Joshua-Fury is 'signed, sealed, delivered', says Hearn

Saudi boxing chief Turki Alalshikh had already turbo-charged speculation on Monday that the fight between Joshua and Fury had been agreed when he posted on social media: "To my friends in Great Britain. It's happening, it's signed."

Hearn echoed Alashikh's sentiment in a post on Instagram shortly after, claiming the paperwork is "Signed, sealed, delivered! AJ vs Fury is on!"

Ring magazine have also confirmed the fight as a "done deal" on X, claiming that the fight will take place in "Q4" of 2026.

Joshua had a pre-existing contract for the fight with Fury - with the latter confirming that he had signed his side of the paperwork after his recent victory against Arslanbek Makhmudov.

"I've signed. I signed months ago. I don't know if he signed," Fury said after the fight at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Hearn's announcement, though, appears to confirm that all parties are now agreement that the fight is officially happening.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury grabbed the mic and bellowed a challenge for Anthony Joshua to fight him next, but failed to get a clear answer from his rival.

Hearn had previously told Sky Sports: "July and November are the two dates that have been presented to us now and we expect to move forward.

"Fury has just had his tune-up fight with 12 really vital rounds to get him sharp for the next one and I expect us to do the same."

Joshua finally accepts Fury's challenge

After Fury outpointed Arslanbek Makhmudov at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium he directly called on Joshua to fight him next.

"I want you, AJ, Anthony Joshua. Let's give the fight fans what they want - the Battle of Britain. I challenge you Anthony Joshua to fight me the Gypsy King next," Fury declared.

"Do you accept my challenge?"

Joshua answered: "I've been chasing you the last 10 years, when you're ready you come and see me and tell me your terms and conditions.

"I'm the boss, you work for me. I'm the landlord. You work for me."

Whether or not Joshua prevails against Prenga, he now looks set to fight Fury in an era-defining bout that will undoubtedly be one of the biggest in British boxing history.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 'AJ will beat Fury!' | Usyk on 'helping' Joshua in camp

Who is Kristian Prenga and what's his record?

Albania's Kristian Prenga is based in the USA and has good record on paper, 20 victories against just one defeat.

Every one of those professional wins has come inside the distance too.

The lone loss on his ledger came early in his career, against then 1-2 Giovanni Auriemma in 2017.

Prenga said: "Anthony Joshua is a great fighter, but he made a terrible miscalculation in picking me as his opponent. This is the kind of fight that changes everything in my life and his.

"I know they have big plans ahead after this fight. I know they are overlooking me. I'm happy about that. I will derail their plans and shock the world this July in Saudi Arabia."

"I mean no disrespect but Kristian Prenga is probably the most googled athlete in the last hour - because, on the surface of things, he's not the best known heavyweight," says Sky Sports Boxing expert Andy Scott.

"But nobody is pretending that this is anything other than an Anthony Joshua test-the-water comeback fight, because he was involved in the terrible car crash that took the life of his two great friends, Sina [Ghami] and Latz [Adoyele]. These were two close friends.

"He's gone through the physical trauma of the car accident. He has to go back into camp, which he has done, and he's taking it slow.

"This will be the test to see how he gets on in the training camp, hard sparring, and the pressure of a big fight week.

"In Saudi Arabia, it will be a more low-profile return for Joshua. It's a fight that they've made that he should win."

Sports.title: Kane needs 'Ballon d'Or moment' with Bayern or England to define his legacy
Sports.content:
Harry Kane had a rest at the weekend but it did not last as long as Vincent Kompany might have hoped. He was pressed into action with Bayern Munich three down to Mainz at half-time. Shortly afterwards, the England captain scored the winner to make it 4-3.

It was goal number 33 for the Bundesliga season. Kompany's sparing use of the striker has all but ended hope of breaking Robert Lewandowski's all-time scoring record for a single Bundesliga season but Kane will still finish as top scorer for a third year running.

That will mean only Lewandowski and Gerd Muller will have been Bundesliga top scorer more times than Kane in the competition's history. It is absurd that Kane's record is rivalling these out-and-out strikers given that he brings much more to this Bayern side.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights as Harry Kane helped turn the game around for Bayern Munich against Mainz

In a recent interview in El Pais, de facto Bayern chief Uli Hoeness articulated this perfectly by setting out what makes Kane different to the rest. "If I look at Bayern over the years, we have always had number nines who scored goals," explained Hoeness.

"When I look at Kane now, I see a number nine like I have never seen before. He defends, organizes, assists, scores goals. Gerd lived in the box. Harry has shifted the number nine's role beyond the box, without neglecting the essence of scoring goals."

It is extraordinary, really. Kane has had twice as many touches of the ball inside his own half than he has within 30 yards of the opposition net. And yet, he is still nine clear in the race for the European Golden Boot in a competition with fewer matches in it.

At the last European Championship, fitness issues saw him substituted with the result in the balance in the semi-final and the final. The hope is that he is better placed now to seize the moment, whether that is for club or country, in the coming weeks and months.

Will Kane edge out Ousmane Dembele as he did Kylian Mbappe in the last round? Maybe crush Arsenal's dreams in the Champions League final in Budapest next month in a moment Tottenham fans would savour every bit as much as the Bayern supporters?

Sports.title: Sabalenka defeats Osaka in Madrid Open thriller
Sports.content:
World No 1 Aryna Sabalenka outgunned four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka in a lung-busting Mutua Madrid Open thriller on Monday.

Sabalenka, a three-time champion in Madrid, reached her fifth quarter-final in Madrid, and a 15th consecutive victory.

The Belarusian recorded a 6-7 (1-7) 6-3 6-2 success against former world No 1 Osaka in an entertaining encounter.

From a set and a break down, Sabalenka did what she does best

✅15th consecutive win, ninth straight win in Madrid



✅23 wins, one loss in Madrid since 2023



✅Fourth straight Madrid quarter-final



✅26-1 in 2026



"That was an incredible level," admitted Sabalenka. "She played really incredible tennis and I feel like I just got lucky with a couple of shots in the third set which is why is kind of felt it went really fast, but overall it was a really incredible fight.

"I'm happy that she brought her fight. I had to fight through and level up my game. I'm happy with my performance."

On Osaka, Sabalenka added: "She's such an inspiration and coming back from pregnancy in a sport like tennis, it's not easy!

"To see her back, for sure she's going to be top 10. It's incredible, it's inspiring. She gives all of us hope that you can go and have a baby, come back, and still play that level of tennis."
